analysis.title: "Optimism In Pockets, Vigilance Warranted": Goldman Says The AI Boom Now Lives Or Dies In The Credit Market
key_insights: Privorotsky (GS EMEA delta-one desk) says AI demand is not the problem. The debate is how much to discount future cash flows given uncertainty around supply, competition and financing.

Privorotsky says the cost of capital has 'objectively repriced' with 'no obvious solve'. Market willingness to supply capital and at what price is the key thing to watch. AI credit spreads came off Friday's wides.

Privorotsky concedes the market may be too flippant about compute oversupply into 2027/28, which could mean excess capacity, structurally lower returns and lower multiples. He says any sustained relief in credit would be a powerful catalyst.
Ramp data flagged by GS TMT desk shows enterprise token spending has barely grown for two months while token volumes keep rising, as cheaper and more efficient models absorb usage growth.

Hatzius chart (Exhibit 4): the year-over-year change in hyperscaler investment as a share of US GDP peaks at roughly 1.5% in Q4 2026 and falls to roughly 0.6% by end of 2027 on consensus estimates. Hatzius sees the AI growth impulse peaking late 2026 or early 2027.
Hatzius estimates the roughly 100bp rise in DM long-end yields this year adds a cumulative 0.6% of GDP drag, only partly in Goldman's forecasts.

Meta financing plan per Sheridan: roughly $35 billion of immediate underwritten offerings plus a roughly $60 billion at-the-market program in a new non-voting Class C share. Bloomberg puts the total at up to $97.5 billion, and the common stock deal was upsized to $25 billion from $22.5 billion.
GS TMT desk notes Meta has turned free-cash-flow negative and its CDS widened. Sheridan reiterated Buy and a $885 price target with no change for dilution.

Privorotsky's four financing scenarios: worst is capex accelerating funded by expensive debt, arguably worse is capex cut because financing is unavailable, best is capex rising with accelerating organic cash flow, and the middle ground is capex flat/up with more equity financing, which is bad for hyperscaler equity and potentially good for credit.

Lynam (GS chief credit strategist) puts off-balance-sheet leases and purchase commitments across five leading hyperscalers at $2.8 trillion, an eightfold increase since 2023. Some companies are talking about securing capital before the market saturates. Meta has a $628 billion off-balance-sheet 'footnote'.

Privorotsky says front-end rates have stabilized, which is good for risk, and energy is too high but more likely to produce chop than a sustained selloff. He calls credit the one to worry about, 'still flashing yellow to red relative to equities'.

Credit stress is concentrated in neoclouds. Bernstein found a $76 billion funding hole at CoreWeave. Per CoinDesk, JPMorgan's private bank says one unnamed debt-laden AI infrastructure firm has 5Y CDS at 1,100bp. Elon Musk warned most of the 200+ neoclouds face 'guppy-level death'.

Overnight rally framed by Privorotsky as an oversold QQQ bounce or the start of something more sustainable. Weeks ahead of major political events (midterms) tend to be constructive. Flows were a little more supportive, with European clients who were net sellers of tech stepping in.

Coppersmith (GS) sees a relief rally as base case given the scale of the hedge fund unwind but prefers call spreads over outright longs because gross leverage is elevated and systematic flows are still negative.
JPMorgan's Andrew Tyler (via Bloomberg): nothing approaching a full-scale return to risk-on, and no one has incentive to be a hero ahead of a big week.

Privorotsky's four hyperscaler tests this week: capex (flat/up fine, down disastrous for picks and shovels), backlog conversion to revenue, FCF conversion in out quarters, and financing mix (equity vs debt). Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday, Amazon Thursday, with the Fed in between.

Overnight supply-side prints: Celestica surged about 17% after hours after guiding to $40 billion of 2027 revenue (up 90% YoY), Cadence beat and raised with $8.2 billion backlog, and Korean memory names rose (Hynix +5%, Samsung +4%, KOSPI +3%).

Financing stress is concentrated here, with lenders pulling back and CDS and funding-gap warnings.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand is robust: AWS 2026 capacity sold out, Celestica guiding $40 billion 2027 revenue, Cadence backlog $8.2 billion, and any sustained relief in credit would be a powerful catalyst.
tension_points.bear_case: Cost of capital has repriced, CCC spreads are at 1,118bp, the AI capex impulse to GDP peaks in Q4 2026, token spend is flat, and compute oversupply into 2027/28 could cut returns and multiples.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hyperscaler capex cut this week (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon), or credit spreads continuing to widen with no relief.

tension_points.bull_case: Equity financing is the middle ground: potentially good for credit, and hyperscaler businesses are strong enough to choose equity over debt.
tension_points.bear_case: Equity issuance is bad for hyperscaler equity, Meta is FCF negative with wider CDS, and the alternative is expensive debt or capex cuts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon following Meta to the equity window would relieve credit. If they do not, the funding burden stays on a credit market with CCCs above 1,100bp.
